context: A welcome talk for new international students at Kingsmead University

cues.t: Part 2. You will hear a student adviser giving a welcome talk to new international students at a university. First you have some time to look at questions 11 to 15.
Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 15.

Hello, everybody, and welcome to Kingsmead University. I'm Greg Mason from the Student Support Office, and over the next few minutes I'll try to answer the questions that new students ask us most often.

The first thing on your list should be enrolment. You've probably filled in the online form already, but that's only the first stage. And there's no need to visit your department about this. To complete your enrolment, you must come in person to the Great Hall before Friday, and you must bring your passport with you.
The queues are usually shortest in the mornings, so try to arrive early. The staff will check your documents, take your photograph and answer any questions you may have about your visa.

Once you've enrolled, you'll be given a student card. It isn't a bus pass, so if you want cheap travel, you'll need to apply to the bus company separately. You can't use it to pay for meals either, although we're hoping to introduce that next year. But do carry it with you at all times, because you can't get into the library without it.

Every new student is also given a mentor, who's a second-year student from your own department. Your mentor can't advise you on which modules to take, as that's your tutor's job, and they won't correct your essays. They're there to help you with everyday things, like how to register with a doctor, where to shop, and how the laundry works.
Your mentor will get in touch with you by email this week, so do look out for that message. Most mentors arrange to meet their students for a coffee in the first few days.

Many of you will be interested in our free English classes. These are open to all students, whatever level you're studying at. They last for one term only, and because everyone has to take a placement test first, they don't start until week three.
The test takes about an hour, and you can sign up for it at the Language Centre.

Finally, a word about money. I wouldn't advise looking for a part-time job in your first term, while you're still settling in. And you can open a bank account during your first week here, so there's no need to worry about that in advance. My main piece of advice is this. Don't buy new textbooks. They're extremely expensive, and the Students' Union runs a second-hand book sale during the first fortnight.
Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 16 to 20.
Now listen and answer questions 16 to 20.

Now, let's see how to find your way around. Please look at the campus map. The main gate is on the east side of the campus, on the right of your map, and University Avenue runs straight ahead of you from there, from east to west.
As you pass through the gate, the first building on your left is the Students' Union. Opposite it, on your right, is the administration block.
The Union has a shop, a café and a large common room, and it's the best place to go if you want to join a club or a society.

Carry on along the avenue until you reach the library, which is the large building on the north side. Directly across the avenue from the library, you'll find the Health Centre, so that's where to go if you need to see a nurse.
If you keep walking, the avenue comes to an end at the Sports Hall, right on the western edge of the campus. Membership is free for all students in their first year.
The campus bookshop is a little harder to find. Take the footpath that runs along the side of the library, and you'll see the shop to the north of the library, facing the back of the building.
It stays open until six o'clock during the first two weeks of term.

And lastly, the Language Centre, where the English classes are held. Go back to the Health Centre and follow the footpath round the lake. The Language Centre stands on the southern shore, with a lovely view across the water.
If you do get lost, just ask anyone wearing a yellow Welcome Team T-shirt. They'll be around the campus all week.
That is the end of Part 2. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

options.B: Find a part-time job as soon as possible.
options.C: Open a bank account before arriving.

groups.limit: Write the correct letter, A–H, next to Questions 16–20.
